data.text:
Lots of people discuss immigration & crime in Europe, so I compiled what I think is ALL the data on the topic, which is hard because many countries hide it.
Do they commit more crime?
Is it because of age? Sex? Education? Poverty? Culture?

1. Sexual offenses & violent crime: https://t.co/EhM15S4O5U

2. GERMANY
Here, Algerians get the record, with one crime for every 3 Algerians every year https://t.co/UTtS8MMsd6

As you can see, many of the top crime origin countries are Muslim, but there can be a confounding factor here, as many Muslim countries are poor & education is low

So I looked into this, and immigrants from Muslim countries commit ~50% more crime than from non-Muslim ones https://t.co/VPFx8xpKju

3. DENMARK
Similar pattern. Here, for violent crime.
MENAPT means Middle East, North Africa, Pakistan, and Turkey. Why that is a statistical region, I'll leave to the reader https://t.co/jxz61xDLxf

Common counterargument: "Yeah but a majority of immigrants are young men. Youth & men commit more crime than the average"

Of course, that means maybe Europe should take that into consideration when accepting immigrants. But even then, if you control for these, you get this: https://t.co/Pvtbuxf6eo

You might want the breakdown per type of crime, so here it is. In Denmark, the top immigrants in terms of crime are Somalians, who are 10-30x more criminal than the average Dane. Meaning for every crime a Dane commits, a Somalian commits 10 to 30 crimes https://t.co/C2vrfE6TGv

Another common counterargument: "Immigrants get profiled more by the police!"

If this were true, we should see lots of arrests but few convictions➡️low conviction rate.

We see the opposite: immigrants tend to be convicted at a much higher rate https://t.co/AgGCjVKgdW

4. SWEDEN
Data is sparser here, but we still see a similar pattern https://t.co/AnFs1cEp5j

5. SPAIN
It's an interesting one because northern European countries tend to attract Muslim immigration, whereas Spain has Muslim, Latin American, and European immigration. https://t.co/Wtd2OXsYt7
So how does crime rate compare per country of origin? Spain doesn't share this data, but we have something else: https://t.co/CMfHZNasnI
6. FINLAND https://t.co/bmRK7dHIoP
7. ITALY https://t.co/kmNdyaFkOk
8. NORWAY https://t.co/sB0RRPRMV5

9. UK
It doesn't share data at the national level, but we have some on sex offenses for London: https://t.co/ULYY2hK4A9
And we have arrests in England and Wales: https://t.co/UxouSHXeJk

When you get deep into the data, you realize a few things that resolve most debates:
1. In fact, in a lot of countries, overall crime rates are down! But it's because the native population gets older (so less crime), compensated by the influx of immigrants, who commit more crime

2. Immigrants don't commit more of all crimes. They specialize in sex crimes & violent assaults

But these are rare crimes compared to, say, pickpocketing

The result is that total crime stats (made disproportionately of petty crimes) can seem stable, while violent crime grows https://t.co/lQGjiKvvO8
3. It's true that the higher crime rate of immigrants is in part due to age, sex, economics & education. But even controlling for those, European immigrants commit much more crime than natives
4. A pretty big tell is that most European countries don't publish all the relevant data—they know that, if they did, the truth would be inconvenient.

But not all immigration is bad:
• The majority of immigrants don't commit crimes
• Many countries provide low-crime immigrants
• Including from Muslim countries: eg, Malaysia, Indonesia
• A good immigrant can come from anywhere. The EU must be able to tell good vs bad ones

Yet at the same time, it is unequivocal that immigrants in Europe cause a lot more crime than natives, which changes the behavior in the country. European countries must be much more selective about their immigrants, and eject the criminals more effectively.

Tomorrow I'll post the same data, but on the economics of immigrants in Europe: What is their contribution?
